title: Tooling: 1.69× faster production R439 omission atlas via packed lanes with identical certificates
body:
## Change and scope

At base `0b1cccf86e2f5132ed286a26ef0a681a495740ea`, production `research/r439-omission-atlas-seed81/verify.py` still replayed every single-ADD omission with a fresh 661-bit row map. Sagar Thakrar’s opt-in adapter `research/omission-lanes-seed92/` (incorporated [#1433](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1433)) already proved sixteen independent omissions in integer bit lanes with identical complete certificates. This PR wires that equivalent rewrite into the **production** PR1017 atlas used by R439 omission tooling.

The historical per-omission `replay(gates,k)` helper is retained for baseline and witness checks. Dependent packages that live-pinned the pairwise-era atlas digest are demoted or refreshed: opt-in `omission-lanes-seed92` vendors pairwise `baseline.py`; `r439-three-omission-distance` demotes its atlas `verify.py` / README pins to provenance (it has its own independent replay). Leave-alone tooling through [#2412](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2412) and deferred `ck-dyadic-replay-production` / `scalar-fused-dyadic-production` were not reopened.

No certificate κ pins change.

**Tooling improvement; no new kappa.** Selected frontier untouched.

## Result

On Linux / CPython 3.12.3 with `taskset -c 0`, five alternating fresh-process pairs over the complete 5,563-mutant atlas gave median wall time **3.630 → 2.143 s (1.694×)**. Timing is host-descriptive and is not a correctness gate. Every honest receipt matches `research/r439-omission-atlas-seed81/CERTIFICATE.json`.

Package: `research/omission-lanes-production/`.
Tip: `c36bb5355b97ee82bb2ee0f28b3214fa4583cafb`.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/omission-lanes-production/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -B research/omission-lanes-production/verify.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/omission-lanes-production
taskset -c 0 python3.12 -I -B research/omission-lanes-production/benchmark.py --rounds 5
```

Expected:

```text
PASS_OMISSION_LANES_PRODUCTION honest=1 matrices=5563 short_checks=7820 corruption=1 certs=1 no_new_kappa
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/omission-lanes-production outcome=completed
PASS_IDENTICAL_OMISSION_LANES_PRODUCTION_RECEIPTS
```

Default verify is read-only. Temp-copy packed-mutant bit-flip foil rejects via audit failure. Package gates under `-O` still load checkers with `compile(..., optimize=0)`. Full `make verify`, selected cold replay, Lean, and multiplication-theorem obligations were not rerun for this isolated historical-checker change.

## Why the packed lanes are equivalent

Pack a batch of `B` omissions as width-`N` lanes inside one Python integer. Lane `j` occupies bits `[jN, (j+1)N)`. An ADD is an XOR of source into destination; XOR cannot carry across lanes. Suppressing lane `j` at omitted gate `k` is exactly the historical `if k != omit` guard for that lane. See `research/omission-lanes-seed92/`.

## Overlap and credit

Closest priors (different delivery): Sagar Thakrar’s `research/omission-lanes-seed92/` / [#1433](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1433) (opt-in packed lanes; this is the production wiring), [CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#756](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/756). Leave-alone tooling through [#2412](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2412) and deferred `ck-dyadic-replay-production` / `scalar-fused-dyadic-production` were not reopened. No competing open PR on production `r439-omission-atlas-seed81/verify.py` at refresh.

Credit woklerx and Sagar Thakrar. Prepared by Wentao Li ([VictorLiwentao](https://github.com/VictorLiwentao), [@Is__Victor](https://x.com/Is__Victor)) with substantial AI assistance, under Apache-2.0.
